title: Boolean Predicates & Single-Pass Partitioning (lists:all/2, lists:any/2, lists:partition/2)
solutionExplanation: Implements collection validation using lists:all/2 and lists:any/2 with short-circuiting, and single-pass order splitting via lists:partition/2.

otpDocCards.description: Returns true if Pred returns true for all elements in List. Short-circuits on first false. Returns true for [].
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) worst-case time, short-circuit O(1) best-case.

otpDocCards.description: Partitions List into two lists based on whether Pred evaluates to true or false in a single pass.

mentalModelCheck.question: What is the return value of lists:all(fun(X) -> X > 10 end, []) and why?

options.label: true, because of the mathematical principle of vacuous truth: no element exists that violates the predicate
options.explanation: In formal predicate calculus, the universal quantification over an empty set evaluates to true.

options.label: false, because there are no elements to satisfy the condition
options.explanation: lists:any returns false on empty lists; lists:all returns true.

options.label: It raises a badarg exception because empty lists are invalid inputs for predicates
options.explanation: Empty lists are standard valid inputs for all collection predicates in stdlib.
